`lm` for linear model - `glmnet` for regularized regression - `keras` for regression using TensorFlow - `stan` for Bayesian regression - `spark` for large data sets - `brulee` for regression using torch ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} . . . - Choose a [model type]{.underline} - Specify an engine - Set the mode ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} logistic_reg() #> Logistic Regression Model Specification (classification) #> #> Computational engine: glm ``` ::: :::notes Models have default engines ::: ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} - Choose a model type - Specify an [engine]{.underline} - Set the mode ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} logistic_reg() |> set_engine("glmnet") #> Logistic Regression Model Specification (classification) #> #> Computational engine: glmnet ``` ::: ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} logistic_reg() |> set_engine("stan") #> Logistic Regression Model Specification (classification) #> #> Computational engine: stan ``` ::: ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} - Choose a model type - Specify an engine - Set the [mode]{.underline} ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} decision_tree() #> Decision Tree Model Specification (unknown mode) #> #> Computational engine: rpart ``` ::: :::notes Some models have a default mode ::: ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") #> Decision Tree Model Specification (classification) #> #> Computational engine: rpart ``` ::: . . .

::: r-fit-text All available models are listed at ::: ## {background-iframe="https://www.tidymodels.org/find/parsnip/"} ::: footer ::: ## To specify a model ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} - Choose a [model type]{.underline} - Specify an [engine]{.underline} - Set the [mode]{.underline} ## Your turn {transition="slide-in"} ![](images/parsnip-flagger.jpg){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="150" height="150"} *Run the `tree_spec` chunk in your `.qmd`.* *Edit this code to use a logistic regression model.*

::: r-fit-text All available models are listed at :::

*Extension/Challenge: Edit this code to use a different model. For example, try using a conditional inference tree as implemented in the partykit package by changing the engine - or try an entirely different model type!* ::: {.cell} ::: ## Models we'll be using today * Logistic regression * Decision trees ::: {.cell} ::: ## Logistic regression ::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-rates-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: ::: ## Logistic regression ::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-logistic-reg-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: ::: ## Logistic regression ::: columns ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-logistic-reg-2-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} - Logit of outcome probability modeled as linear combination of predictors: $log(\frac{p}{1 - p}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\cdot \text{A}$ - Find a sigmoid line that separates the two classes ::: ::: ## Decision trees ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-fit-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: ::: ## Decision trees ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-fit-2-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - Series of splits or if/then statements based on predictors - First the tree *grows* until some condition is met (maximum depth, no more data) - Then the tree is *pruned* to reduce its complexity ::: ::: ## Decision trees ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-fit-3-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-preds-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## All models are wrong, but some are useful! ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Logistic regression ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-logistic-reg-3-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Decision tree ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-preds-2-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: ## In two dimensions ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Logistic regression ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-logistic-reg-2d-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Decision tree ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-preds-2d-1.svg) ::: ::: ::: ::: # A model workflow ## Workflows bind preprocessors and models ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](images/good_workflow.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: :::notes Explain that PCA that is a preprocessor / dimensionality reduction, used to decorrelate data ::: ## What is wrong with this? {.annotation}
::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](images/bad_workflow.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: :::notes The source of data leakage here is preprocessing on the whole source data set rather than on the whole training set. So, the risk is "the values from the test set affect the mean and standard deviations used in the preprocessing." That discussion shouldn't mention metrics, as they haven't been introduced yet. While centering + scaling are easy to explain the general idea with, it's not necessarily the biggest danger in practice. The more elaborate the estimation in your preprocessing, the higher the risk of overfitting coming back to bite you. An example of a more elaborate preprocessing estimation is principal components. ::: ## Why a `workflow()`? ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} . . . - Workflows handle new data better than base R tools in terms of new factor levels . . . - You can use other preprocessors besides formulas . . . - They can help organize your work when working with multiple models . . . - [Most importantly]{.underline}, a workflow captures the entire modeling process: `fit()` and `predict()` apply to the pre/post processing steps in addition to the actual model fit ::: notes Two ways workflows handle levels better than base R: - Enforces that new levels are not allowed at prediction time (this is an optional check that can be turned off) - Restores missing levels that were present at fit time, but happen to be missing at prediction time (like, if your "new" data just doesn't have an instance of that level) ::: ## A model workflow ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tree_spec <- decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") tree_spec |> fit(class ~ ., data = cls_train) #> parsnip model object #> #> n= 800 #> #> node), split, n, loss, yval, (yprob) #> * denotes terminal node #> #> 1) root 800 266 class_1 (0.66750000 0.33250000) #> 2) pred_2< 0.3297983 510 30 class_1 (0.94117647 0.05882353) * #> 3) pred_2>=0.3297983 290 54 class_2 (0.18620690 0.81379310) #> 6) pred_1>=1.236161 71 28 class_1 (0.60563380 0.39436620) #> 12) pred_2< 1.476946 42 7 class_1 (0.83333333 0.16666667) * #> 13) pred_2>=1.476946 29 8 class_2 (0.27586207 0.72413793) #> 26) pred_1>=2.070158 7 2 class_1 (0.71428571 0.28571429) * #> 27) pred_1< 2.070158 22 3 class_2 (0.13636364 0.86363636) * #> 7) pred_1< 1.236161 219 11 class_2 (0.05022831 0.94977169) * ``` ::: ## A model workflow ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tree_spec <- decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") workflow() |> add_formula(class ~ .) |> add_model(tree_spec) |> fit(data = cls_train) #> ══ Workflow [trained] ════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Preprocessor: Formula #> Model: decision_tree() #> #> ── Preprocessor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> class ~ . #> #> ── Model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> n= 800 #> #> node), split, n, loss, yval, (yprob) #> * denotes terminal node #> #> 1) root 800 266 class_1 (0.66750000 0.33250000) #> 2) pred_2< 0.3297983 510 30 class_1 (0.94117647 0.05882353) * #> 3) pred_2>=0.3297983 290 54 class_2 (0.18620690 0.81379310) #> 6) pred_1>=1.236161 71 28 class_1 (0.60563380 0.39436620) #> 12) pred_2< 1.476946 42 7 class_1 (0.83333333 0.16666667) * #> 13) pred_2>=1.476946 29 8 class_2 (0.27586207 0.72413793) #> 26) pred_1>=2.070158 7 2 class_1 (0.71428571 0.28571429) * #> 27) pred_1< 2.070158 22 3 class_2 (0.13636364 0.86363636) * #> 7) pred_1< 1.236161 219 11 class_2 (0.05022831 0.94977169) * ``` ::: ## A model workflow ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tree_spec <- decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") workflow(class ~ ., tree_spec) |> fit(data = cls_train) #> ══ Workflow [trained] ════════════════════════════════════════════════ #> Preprocessor: Formula #> Model: decision_tree() #> #> ── Preprocessor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> class ~ . #> #> ── Model ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> n= 800 #> #> node), split, n, loss, yval, (yprob) #> * denotes terminal node #> #> 1) root 800 266 class_1 (0.66750000 0.33250000) #> 2) pred_2< 0.3297983 510 30 class_1 (0.94117647 0.05882353) * #> 3) pred_2>=0.3297983 290 54 class_2 (0.18620690 0.81379310) #> 6) pred_1>=1.236161 71 28 class_1 (0.60563380 0.39436620) #> 12) pred_2< 1.476946 42 7 class_1 (0.83333333 0.16666667) * #> 13) pred_2>=1.476946 29 8 class_2 (0.27586207 0.72413793) #> 26) pred_1>=2.070158 7 2 class_1 (0.71428571 0.28571429) * #> 27) pred_1< 2.070158 22 3 class_2 (0.13636364 0.86363636) * #> 7) pred_1< 1.236161 219 11 class_2 (0.05022831 0.94977169) * ``` ::: ## Your turn {transition="slide-in"} ![](images/parsnip-flagger.jpg){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="150" height="150"} *Run the `tree_wflow` chunk in your `classwork-03-what-makes-a-model.qmd`.* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tree_spec <- decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") tree_wflow <- workflow() |> add_formula(class ~ .) |> add_model(tree_spec) tree_wflow ``` ::: *Edit this code to make a workflow with your own model of choice.*
*Extension/Challenge: Other than formulas, what kinds of preprocessors are supported?* ::: {.cell} ::: ## Predict with your model ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} How do you use your new `tree_fit` model? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tree_spec <- decision_tree() |> set_mode("classification") tree_fit <- workflow(class ~ ., tree_spec) |> fit(data = cls_train) ``` ::: ## Your turn {transition="slide-in"} ![](images/parsnip-flagger.jpg){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="150" height="150"} *Run:* `predict(tree_fit, new_data = cls_test)` *What do you notice about the structure of the result?* ::: {.cell} ::: ## Your turn ![](images/parsnip-flagger.jpg){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="150" height="150"} *Run:* `augment(tree_fit, new_data = cls_test)` *How does the output compare to the output from `predict()`?* ::: {.cell} ::: # The tidymodels prediction guarantee! . . . - The predictions will always be inside a **tibble** - The column names and types are **unsurprising** and **predictable** - The number of rows in `new_data` and the output **are the same** ## Understand your model ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} {.annotation} How do you **understand** your new `tree_fit` model? ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](figures/plot-tree-fit-4-1.svg){fig-align='center'} ::: ::: ## Understand your model ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} How do you **understand** your new `tree_fit` model? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(rpart.plot) tree_fit |> extract_fit_engine() |> rpart.plot() ``` ::: You can `extract_*()` several components of your fitted workflow. . . . ⚠️ *Never `predict()` with any extracted components!* ::: notes `roundint = FALSE` is only to quiet a warning ::: ## {background-iframe="https://hardhat.tidymodels.org/reference/hardhat-extract.html"} ::: footer ::: ## Understand your model ![](hexes/workflows.png){.absolute top=-20 right=0 width="64" height="74.24"} ![](hexes/parsnip.png){.absolute top=-20 right=64 width="64" height="74.24"} How do you **understand** your new `tree_fit` model? . . . You can use your fitted workflow for model and/or prediction explanations: . . . - overall variable importance, such as with the [vip](https://koalaverse.github.io/vip/) package . . . - flexible model explainers, such as with the [DALEXtra](https://dalex.drwhy.ai/) package . . . Learn more at ## Your turn {transition="slide-in"} ![](images/parsnip-flagger.jpg){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="150" height="150"}
*Extract the model engine object from your fitted workflow and check it out.* ::: {.cell} ::: :::notes Afterward, ask what kind of object people got from the extraction, and what they did with it (e.g. give it to `summary()`, `plot()`, `broom::tidy()` ). Live code along ::: ## The whole game - status update ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](images/whole-game-transparent-model-1.jpg){fig-align='center' width=3543} ::: ::: :::notes Stress that fitting a model on the entire training set was only for illustrating how to fit a model :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
